newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends week lower in gloomy trading.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends week lower in gloomy trading.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended the week on Friday 0.48 percent lower, led down by large capitalisation firms, including Societe Nationale d'Investissement, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 666.61 points from 669.83 points, last Friday.
"The market is gloomy with low volumes traded on the official market along with downward corrections in stocks which rose steadily for more than three months," a broker said.
ONA Group , Morocco's largest private conglomerate, fell five dirhams on the week to close at 800 dirhams, compared with 805 dirhams last week. About 14,818 ONA shares were traded on the week.
SNI, the second largest private conglomerate, closed at 725 dirhams from 760 dirhams last Friday. About 11,876 shares were exchanged on the week.
Mortgage firm Credit Hotelier et Immobilier closed at 275 dirhams from 300 dirhams.
Cement firm Lafarge Ciments closed at 1,315 dirhams from 1,351 last week.
In the banking sector, Wafabank dropped 10 dirhams to 850 dirhams from 860 dirhams last Friday. Banque Commerciale du Maroc, shed six dirhams to 864 dirhams.
Samir, Morocco's main oil refinery, which was recently privatised, closed at 377.20 dirhams from 326.50 dirhams ($34.7).
Total volume on the official market fell to 32.1 million from 77.4 million dirhams last Friday.
Volume on the official market was 186.2 million dirhams from 43.6 million dirhams last Friday, a bourse official said.
